definition_zh: 也许；或许；可能；大概
definition_en: used to say that something may be true or may happen, or to make a suggestion, request or estimate sound softer
core_image: 一枚硬币还在空中旋转，正反两面都还握在手里
scene: 雨点敲着窗，朋友问晚上要不要出门，你还没有拿定主意。Perhaps we should stay in and cook something simple.
sceneCN: 这里是「也许、可能」（第 1 个义项：表示不确定的可能性）；句意为也许今晚该待在家里做点简单的饭菜。

derivatives.zh: 与 perhaps 共享表示「运气、机会」的词干 hap，义为「发生；碰巧」
hap 加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「小事故；不幸」，与 perhaps 同源
hap 与 hazard 复合，义为「偶然的；杂乱的」，与 perhaps 同源

senses.title: Something may be true or may happen
senses.definition: used to say that something may be the case or may happen, without saying that it will
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事可能是真的或可能发生，但并不保证会发生
senses.example: Perhaps the train is late because of the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 也许火车是因为下雪才晚点的。
senses.why: The word began as a phrase meaning by chance, so its first job is to mark a possibility sitting between yes and no.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是「凭运气」的说法，所以它最基本的用途是标出一种停在「是」与「否」之间的可能性。

senses.title: A softened request or suggestion
senses.definition: used to make a suggestion, request or opinion sound less direct and less forceful
senses.definitionCN: 用于让建议、请求或看法听起来不那么直接、不那么强硬
senses.example: Perhaps you could send the file before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 或许你可以在周五之前把文件发过来。
senses.why: If a claim only describes a chance, the speaker cannot be accused of pushing too hard, so the same word becomes a polite way to ask for something.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个说法只描述「有可能」，说话人就不算把话说满，于是同一个词变成了客气地提出请求的方式。

senses.title: An approximate number
senses.definition: used before a number to show that it is an estimate rather than an exact figure
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字前，表示那是估出来的数目而非精确数字
senses.example: Perhaps forty people came to the talk.
senses.exampleCN: 大概有四十个人来听了那场讲座。
senses.why: An estimate is just a possible figure rather than a measured one, which is the same hedge applied to quantity instead of to truth.
senses.whyCN: 估出来的数字只是「可能如此」的数目，而不是量出来的，这等于把同样的不确定从真假挪到了数量上。

intro.en: Perhaps is a worn-down English phrase: a Latin preposition joined to an old Norse noun for luck and written as one word.
intro.cn: perhaps 是一个磨平了的英语短语：一个拉丁语介词接上一个表示运气的古诺斯语名词，最后写成了一个词。

items.en: Latin per meant through or by, and it is still visible in phrases such as per cent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 per 意为「经由、凭」，在 per cent 这类短语里仍能看见。

items.en: Old Norse happ meant chance or good luck, and English kept it as the noun hap.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 happ 意为「机会、好运」，英语把它保留为名词 hap。

items.en: Middle English put the two together as the phrase per hap, literally by chance.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者合为短语 per hap，字面意思就是「凭运气」。

items.en: The phrase was written as one word, first as perhappes or perhapse, before the modern spelling settled.
items.cn: 这个短语被写成一个词，先作 perhappes 或 perhapse，之后才固定成现代拼写。

items.en: Modern English uses perhaps as a single adverb of possibility, while the old noun hap survives mainly inside compounds.
items.cn: 现代英语把 perhaps 当作一个表示可能性的副词，旧名词 hap 主要残留在复合词里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words sharing the old noun for luck; the near-meaning group collects adverbs that also mark possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「运气」这个旧名词的词；近义组收同样标记可能性的副词。

entries.definition: An old word for chance or luck, now rare outside compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 表示机会或运气的古词，如今主要残留在复合词中。

entries.definition: To take place, especially by chance.
entries.definitionCN: 发生，尤指偶然发生。

entries.definition: Arranged without plan or order.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无计划或秩序地安排的；杂乱的。

entries.definition: A small accident or piece of bad luck.
entries.definitionCN: 小事故；不幸的意外。

entries.definition: Possibly; used to say that something may be the case.
entries.definitionCN: 也许；用于表示某事可能如此。

entries.definition: Used when something is possible but not certain.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表示有可能但不确定。

entries.definition: Used when something is more likely than not.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表示可能性较大；很可能。

entries.definition: In a way that can be imagined as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 可以想象为可能的；或许。

normalIntro.en: The word still shows its two pieces: a preposition of means and an old noun for luck.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词至今还露着两块零件：一个表示「凭借」的介词，和一个表示运气的旧名词。

normal.en: Per hap literally says by chance, which is exactly what the adverb still does.
normal.cn: per hap 字面就是「凭运气」，这正是这个副词今天仍在做的事。

normal.en: Hap is an old word for luck, and it lives on in happen, haphazard and mishap.
normal.cn: hap 是表示运气的古词，如今活在 happen、haphazard 和 mishap 里。

normal.en: Latin per means through or by, as in per cent, by the hundred.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 per 意为「经由、凭」，如 per cent 就是「按百计算」。

normal.en: Perhaps and maybe do the same job, but perhaps is the more written and more formal of the two.
normal.cn: perhaps 与 maybe 作用相同，但 perhaps 更偏书面、更正式。

normal.en: At the head of a sentence, perhaps usually softens a suggestion rather than expressing real doubt.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，perhaps 多半是在软化建议，而不是真的表示怀疑。

abstract.en: Keep the coin spinning in the air: while it turns, both faces are still possible, and that is the whole meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象那枚还在空中旋转的硬币：转着的时候正反两面都还可能，这就是这个词的全部意思。

abstract.en: A hedge is not a lie and not a promise, and perhaps is the little hedge people plant around a claim.
abstract.cn: 含糊其辞既不是撒谎也不是承诺，perhaps 就是人们在说法周围种下的一小圈篱笆。

abstract.en: The word costs the speaker almost nothing, yet it leaves room for the listener to disagree without a fight.
abstract.cn: 这个词几乎不花说话人什么代价，却给听者留出了不伤和气地反对的余地。

examples.en: Perhaps the rain will stop before we leave.
examples.cn: 也许我们出发前雨会停。

examples.en: Perhaps you should ask the manager directly.
examples.cn: 或许你该直接去问经理。

examples.en: There were perhaps twenty people in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里大概有二十个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕哈普斯」——心里没底就怕说错，先加一句也许垫着；记住 perhaps 是或许。

root: 中古英语短语 per hap，字面义为「凭运气」；per 来自拉丁语 per（经由），hap 来自古诺斯语 happ（运气、机会），同源词还有 happen、mishap。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a possibility held open; the senses then spread to polite suggestions and to rough estimates of number.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一种悬着不定的可能性；义项由此扩展到委婉的建议和粗略的数字估计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin still spinning in the air, neither face settled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币还在空中旋转，哪一面都还没落定。

branches.en: a coin still spinning in the air
branches.cn: 还在空中旋转的硬币

branches.en: a cloud that may or may not bring rain
branches.cn: 说不准会不会下雨的云

branches.en: a note passed quietly to a colleague
branches.cn: 悄悄递给同事的一张便条

branches.en: a rough count made on the fingers
branches.cn: 用手指粗略点数

branches.en: a forecast that speaks of likely showers
branches.cn: 说可能有阵雨的天气预报

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin preposition of means and an old Norse noun for luck, written as one unit only in English.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示「凭借」的拉丁语介词和一个表示运气的古诺斯语名词拼成，只有英语把它写成了一个单位。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies only the preposition per; the noun hap is Germanic, borrowed from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供了介词 per；名词 hap 属于日耳曼语，借自古诺斯语。

definition_zh: 永久的；长期不变的；常设的；正式编制的；（烫发）保持较久的
definition_en: lasting for a very long time or indefinitely; not temporary
core_image: 石碑上凿出的字，雨水冲了几十年还在
scene: 河岸的界桩深深打进岩层，涨水也没能把它拔起。The border marker is a permanent fixture on the bank.
sceneCN: 这里指长期存在、不会自行消失（第 1 个义项：永久或长期存续的）；句意为这块界标是河岸上永久固定的设施；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 永久的；长期的；常设的；正式编制的

senses.title: Lasting indefinitely
senses.definition: lasting forever or with no fixed end
senses.definitionCN: 永远存在或没有确定终点
senses.example: The treaty made the river a permanent boundary.
senses.exampleCN: 条约使这条河成为永久边界。
senses.why: Latin permanere means to remain through to the end, and the present participle fixes that staying into a quality.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 permanere 意为「一直留到最后」，现在分词把这层「留住」定成品性。

senses.title: Long-lasting rather than temporary
senses.definition: intended to last a long time, in contrast with a temporary arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 打算长期维持，与临时安排相对
senses.example: They moved into a permanent office after the trial year.
senses.exampleCN: 试行一年后，他们搬进了长期办公室。
senses.why: Everyday use softens forever into for the foreseeable future.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法把「永远」软化为「可预见的将来」。

senses.title: A regular staff position
senses.definition: holding a post with a settled contract rather than a short-term one
senses.definitionCN: 持有稳定合同的岗位，而非短期岗位
senses.example: She was offered a permanent post in the department.
senses.exampleCN: 系里给了她一个正式职位。
senses.why: Employment law turns the word into a boundary between contract types.
senses.whyCN: 劳动法把这个词变成合同类型之间的界限。

senses.title: A material that does not fade
senses.definition: marking a material whose colour or mark is meant to stay
senses.definitionCN: 标记一种颜色或印记不易消失的材料
senses.example: He labelled the box with a permanent marker.
senses.exampleCN: 他用不褪色记号笔在箱子上做了标记。
senses.why: The adjective moves from the arrangement to the stuff that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从安排转到承载安排的材质上。

senses.title: A long-holding wave
senses.definition: a hairstyle whose curl is meant to last for months
senses.definitionCN: 卷发效果能维持数月的发型
senses.example: She asked the stylist for a permanent before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出行前她请理发师给她烫个发。
senses.why: The trade noun keeps the promise of duration in a small everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 行业里的名词把「持久」的承诺放进一个日常小义。

senses.title: A resident status
senses.definition: the legal right to live in a country without time limit
senses.definitionCN: 在一国无限期居住的合法权利
senses.example: He applied for permanent residence after five years.
senses.exampleCN: 五年后他申请了永久居留。
senses.why: Immigration law needs a term for the strongest form of stay.
senses.whyCN: 移民法需要一个词指最稳固的居留形式。

senses.title: Irreversible harm
senses.definition: damage that will not heal or be undone
senses.definitionCN: 不会痊愈或被撤销的损害
senses.example: The frost caused permanent damage to the buds.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻对花芽造成了永久性损害。
senses.why: The word marks the point where repair stops being possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出修复不再可能的那一点。

senses.title: A lasting record
senses.definition: an official record that is kept indefinitely
senses.definitionCN: 无限期保存的正式记录
senses.example: The offence stayed on his permanent record.
senses.exampleCN: 这项过错留在了他的永久档案里。
senses.why: Bureaucracy uses the word to say that erasure is not allowed.
senses.whyCN: 行政系统用这个词表示不允许抹除。

intro.en: Permanent comes from Latin permanens, the present participle of permanere, to remain throughout, built on per- through and manere to stay. Both parts are clear.
intro.cn: permanent 来自拉丁 permanens，即 permanere「一直留到最后」的现在分词，由 per-「贯穿」与 manere「停留」构成。两部分都清楚。

items.en: Manere meant to stay, remain or dwell, and it also gives mansion and manor through French.
items.cn: manere 意为停留、留下、居住，经法语也给出 mansion 与 manor。

items.en: Per- means through or throughout, so permanere is to stay through the whole span.
items.cn: per- 意为贯穿、始终，因此 permanere 是在整段时间里一直留下。

items.en: The present participle permanens described a thing that keeps its place or state.
items.cn: 现在分词 permanens 描述保持位置或状态的事物。

items.en: English took permanent in the late Middle Ages; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入 permanent，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Permanence and permanency name the state, while impermanent adds a Latin negative prefix.
items.cn: permanence 与 permanency 命名状态，impermanent 则加拉丁否定前缀。

items.en: The word now also names a hairstyle, a marker and a residence status.
items.cn: 这个词如今还指一种发型、一种记号笔与一种居留身份。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin stay-root; the second group names duration and stability.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「停留」词根；第二组是表示持续与稳定的近义说法。

entries.definition: The state of lasting or remaining unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 持久或保持不变的状态。

entries.definition: In a way that is meant to last.
entries.definitionCN: 以打算长久维持的方式。

entries.definition: Not lasting; the negative form built with im-.
entries.definitionCN: 不持久的；用 im- 构成的否定形式。

entries.definition: To stay behind or continue in a place, from the same Latin verb through French.
entries.definitionCN: 留下或继续在某处，经法语出自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: A large house, from the Latin idea of dwelling.
entries.definitionCN: 大宅，出自拉丁语「居住」的观念。

entries.definition: Continuing for a long time, without implying forever.
entries.definitionCN: 持续很久，但不含「永远」。

entries.definition: Lasting through hardship or time.
entries.definitionCN: 历经困难或时间仍持续。

entries.definition: Continuing without interruption, often stronger than permanent.
entries.definitionCN: 不间断地持续，语气常比 permanent 更强。

entries.definition: Set in place and not changing.
entries.definitionCN: 固定就位、不再改变。

entries.definition: Steady and not likely to move or fail.
entries.definitionCN: 稳定，不易移动或失效。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Manere is to stay, and per- is through, so permanent is to stay through the whole span.
normal.cn: manere 是停留，per- 是贯穿，所以 permanent 是整段时间都留下。

normal.en: Mansion and manor come from the same dwelling word.
normal.cn: mansion 与 manor 出自同一个「居住」词。

normal.en: Impermanent is the negative: im- plus permanent.
normal.cn: impermanent 是反义：im- 加 permanent。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: permanent residence, permanent job, permanent damage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：永久居留、正式工作、永久损害。

normal.en: A permanent marker keeps its mark; a permanent wave keeps its curl.
normal.cn: 不褪色记号笔留住字迹，烫发留住卷度。

abstract.en: Permanent is a stone carved with letters that outlast the hand that cut them.
abstract.cn: 永久是石头上凿的字，比刻字的手活得更久。

abstract.en: The word promises duration without naming an end, which is why lawyers argue over it.
abstract.cn: 这个词承诺持续却不说明终点，所以律师总要争它。

abstract.en: To call a thing permanent is to bet that time will not revise it.
abstract.cn: 称某物为永久，就是赌时间不会改写它。

examples.en: The bridge was built as a permanent crossing, not a seasonal one.
examples.cn: 这座桥建成永久通道，而非季节性设施。

examples.en: A permanent loss of hearing followed the explosion.
examples.cn: 爆炸之后出现了永久性听力丧失。

examples.en: The museum keeps a permanent collection in the east wing.
examples.cn: 博物馆在东翼设有永久藏品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「泼门能特」——门泼上漆也烂不掉：永久的

root: 拉丁 permanens「一直留下的」← permanere「留到最后」← per-「贯穿」+ manere「停留、居住」。manere 经法语也给出 mansion 与 manor；英语中世纪晚期借入 permanent，确切首见年代不确定。permanence 指状态，impermanent 由 im- 否定；现代另有烫发、不褪色记号笔与永久居留等专义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from endless duration to long arrangements, posts, materials, hairstyles, statuses, harm and records.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从无限持续，转到长期安排、职位、材料、发型、身份、损害与档案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: letters cut into stone, still readable after decades of rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：凿进石头的字，几十年雨水之后仍可辨认。

branches.en: THE ENDLESS STAY: duration with no fixed end.
branches.cn: 没有终点的停留：没有确定终点的持续。

branches.en: THE LONG ARRANGEMENT: what is meant to outlast a trial period.
branches.cn: 长期安排：打算熬过试行期的安排。

branches.en: THE SETTLED STATUS: a staff post and a residence right.
branches.cn: 稳固的身份：正式职位与居留权利。

branches.en: THE FIXED MARK: ink that does not fade and a curl that holds.
branches.cn: 固定的印记：不褪的字迹与持久的卷度。

branches.en: THE UNCHANGING RECORD: harm that cannot be undone and a file that is never erased.
branches.cn: 不可改的记录：无法撤销的损害与永不抹除的档案。

intro.en: Permanent is Latin permanens plus the English adjective ending; the verb permanere carries both per- and manere.
intro.cn: permanent 是拉丁 permanens 加英语形容词词尾；动词 permanere 同时带着 per- 与 manere。

latinIntro.en: Manere gives the stay-root, per- carries it through time, and permanens supplies the participle behind the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: manere 提供「停留」词根，per- 让它贯穿时间，permanens 提供英语形容词背后的分词。

items.example: The prefix stretches the stay across the whole span.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把「停留」拉满整段时间。

items.example: The verb is the plain act of remaining.
items.exampleCN: 动词就是「留下」这一平实动作。

items.structure: Latin verb, compound of per- and manere
items.example: Latin joined the two parts into one verb.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把两部分合成一个动词。

items.example: The participle turns the act into a quality.
The noun names the state the participle describes.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名分词所描述的状态。

items.example: English keeps the participle ending as -ent.
items.exampleCN: 英语把分词词尾保留为 -ent。

items.example: The noun is the abstract partner of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 名词是形容词的抽象搭档。

items.example: The adverb marks how long something is meant to stay.
items.exampleCN: 副词标出打算维持多久。

items.example: The prefix makes impermanent, the negative partner.
items.exampleCN: 前缀构成 impermanent 这一否定搭档。

items.example: The negative keeps the same stay-root.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式沿用同一「停留」词根。

definition_zh: 允许；许可；正式批准；书面批文；权限
definition_en: the act of allowing someone to do something, or the official right to do it that an authority grants
core_image: 一把钥匙被放进掌心：门还锁着，但你已经有权把它推开
scene: 美术馆的展厅里，讲解员把三脚架拦在门外，指着墙上一行小字提醒参观者。Photographs are allowed only with written permission from the museum.
sceneCN: 这里是「正式许可、批准」（第 2 个义项：机构给出的正式准许）；句意为只有拿到博物馆的书面许可才能拍照。画面的重点是门口被拦下的三脚架和墙上那行小字。

pos.zh: 允许；许可；批准；书面批文；权限

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 permiss- 加 -ive 构成，义为「宽容的；放任的」
由同一词干加 -ible 构成，义为「可允许的；容许的」
与 permission 同出拉丁语 permittere，作动词指「允许」，作名词指「许可证」；两者同源但不是同一词的词形变化
由 permissive 加 -ness 构成，义为「宽容；放任」

senses.title: The act of allowing someone to do something
senses.definition: the act of agreeing that someone may do something, without necessarily putting it in writing
senses.definitionCN: 同意某人可以做某事的行为，不一定落实为文字
senses.example: She gave me permission to use her desk while she was away.
senses.exampleCN: 她不在的时候允许我用她的桌子。
senses.why: Latin permittere joins per-, through, with mittere, to send or let go; the idea is letting something pass out of your control.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 permittere 由表示「穿过」的 per- 与表示「送出、放开」的 mittere 合成，本义是让某件事从自己的掌控中放行，所以这个词天生带着点头放人的动作感。

senses.title: Official authorization from an authority
senses.definition: the official right to do something that a person or body in authority gives you
senses.definitionCN: 由有权的个人或机构给予的做某事的正式权利
senses.example: No one may film inside the court without permission from the judge.
senses.exampleCN: 未经法官批准，任何人不得在法庭内拍摄。
senses.why: Once the letting-through happens inside an institution, the same noun names the authorization the body issues rather than a private nod.
senses.whyCN: 当「放行」发生在机构内部，这个名词就从私人的点头变成了机构发出的授权，因此在规章语境里它几乎等同于批准。

senses.title: A written or formal grant, often countable
senses.definition: a formal document or stated allowance that records the right to do something
senses.definitionCN: 记录做某事权利的正式文件或明确许可
senses.example: The crew needed three separate permissions to shut the street for a night.
senses.exampleCN: 摄制组需要三份不同的批文才能封街一夜。
senses.why: Permission can be counted when the thing counted is not the consent itself but the separate grants, one for each activity.
senses.whyCN: 当被计数的不是「同意」本身，而是逐项开出的批文时，permission 就可以数了，一次活动一份，于是出现复数形式。

senses.title: Access rights inside a computer system
senses.definition: the rights that control what a user may read, change or delete on a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 控制用户在计算机系统中可以读取、修改或删除哪些内容的权利
senses.example: The folder refuses to open until an administrator changes its permissions.
senses.exampleCN: 在管理员更改文件夹权限之前，它打不开。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the institutional sense literally: the system checks whether your account has been let through to a file.
senses.whyCN: 计算机几乎是照搬机构义的逻辑：系统检查你的账号是否被放行到某个文件，于是同一个词变成了权限设置。

intro.en: Permission descends from Latin permissio, the action noun of permittere; it shares that verb with the English verb permit but is not the verb plus a suffix.
intro.cn: permission 源自拉丁语 permissio，那是动词 permittere 的动作名词；它与英语动词 permit 共享同一个拉丁动词，并不是由 permit 直接加后缀变来的。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it lies under a large Latin family of release and sending.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放开，许多表示释放与送出的拉丁词都由它衍生。

items.en: Adding per-, through, produced permittere, to let something pass through, and therefore to allow it.
items.cn: 加上表示「穿过」的 per-，构成 permittere：让某物通过，因而引申为允许。

items.en: The action noun permissio named the letting-through itself and is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 动作名词 permissio 指放行这件事本身，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as permission and handed it to Middle English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语以 permission 的形式承接这个名词，并在十四世纪交给中古英语。

items.en: English kept the noun for consent, later allowed countable grants, and in the twentieth century added computer access rights.
items.cn: 英语保留名词表示同意的用法，后来发展出可数的批文义，二十世纪又添上计算机访问权一义。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same Latin verb of letting through; the second collects words about consent, approval and access.
note.cn: 第一组收同一个拉丁动词派生出的词；第二组收表示同意、批准与准入的词。

entries.definition: The verb, and separately the noun for a licence, both built on Latin permittere.
entries.definitionCN: 直接建于拉丁语 permittere 之上的动词，以及另一个表示许可证的名词。

entries.definition: Allowing a lot of freedom and not punishing behaviour strictly.
entries.definitionCN: 给予很大自由、不严格约束行为的；宽容的。

entries.definition: Allowed by a rule or by law.
entries.definitionCN: 规则或法律所允许的。

entries.definition: A task someone is sent to carry out, from the Latin verb of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 派某人去完成的任务，出自同一个表示送出的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Agreement to something happening, given by someone free to refuse.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事发生的同意，由有权拒绝的人给出。

entries.definition: Official power or approval to act, usually written down.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的正式权力或批准，通常见诸文字。

entries.definition: Official permission to go ahead, especially after a check.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指经审查后获得的继续进行的正式许可。

entries.definition: A document that allows an activity, usually paid for.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某项活动的证件，通常需要付费取得。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by a Latin verb of letting through, and its relatives keep returning to gates, grants and keys.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词靠一个表示放行的拉丁动词支撑，同族词反复回到门禁、批文与钥匙上。

normal.en: Per- means through in Latin, so permission is literally a letting-through: the gate opens and you walk in.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 per- 意为穿过，所以 permission 字面上就是放行：门开了，你走进去。

normal.en: The noun keeps the miss- stem of mittere, to send; the same stem hides in mission and in the verb permit.
normal.cn: 这个名词保留了 mittere（送出）的 miss- 词干，同一词干也藏在 mission 与动词 permit 里。

normal.en: You ask for permission and you receive permission, and those two verbs box in most of its everyday use.
normal.cn: 请求许可、获得许可，这一对动词几乎框住了它在日常里的全部用法。

normal.en: Without permission and with permission are fixed pairs, and the noun after with takes no article.
normal.cn: 未经许可与经许可都是固定搭配，with 后面直接跟不带冠词的名词。

normal.en: Spoken English often prefers to say that someone is allowed to do something, while written rules prefer the noun.
normal.cn: 口语常说某人被允许做某事，而书面规章更偏爱这个名词。

abstract.en: Permission is a door held open by someone else: the room was always there, but you could not enter until that hand moved.
abstract.cn: permission 是别人替你扶住的门：房间一直在那里，可那只手不动，你就进不去。

abstract.en: The word measures the distance between wanting to do something and being entitled to do it.
abstract.cn: 这个词量出的，是想做某件事与有权做某件事之间的距离。

abstract.en: Inside a computer the same idea becomes a switch: access is either granted or refused, with nothing in between.
abstract.cn: 在计算机里，同一个念头变成一个开关：访问权要么被授予，要么被拒绝，中间没有余地。

examples.en: Nobody leaves the base without written permission.
examples.cn: 没有书面许可，谁也不能离开基地。

examples.en: The council finally gave permission for the market to reopen.
examples.cn: 市政会终于批准市场重新开放。

examples.en: She was refused permission to sit the exam early.
examples.cn: 她提前参加考试的申请被拒绝了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕米审」——想从米仓取米，得先过一道审查，怕米审不过就一粒也拿不走；permission 就是许可。

root: 拉丁语 permittere（per- 穿过 + mittere 送出）意为放行、允许，其名词形 permissio 经古法语 permission 进入英语；同族词多与送出、放行有关。

sensesIntro.en: From a private nod to an official grant and then to a line of code, the word keeps one idea: something is let through.
sensesIntro.cn: 从私人的点头到机构的批准，再到一行代码，这个词始终守着一个意思：某样东西被放行了。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key placed in your palm while the door stays shut until you turn it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把钥匙被放进掌心，门还锁着，等你转动手腕。

branches.en: a friend nodding so you may borrow the chair
branches.cn: 朋友点头，你才把那把椅子搬走

branches.en: a signature at the bottom of an official form
branches.cn: 公文末尾的一个签名

branches.en: the same yes, spoken once and printed once
branches.cn: 同一个「可以」，一次说出口，一次印成纸

branches.en: a locked folder waiting for an administrator
branches.cn: 一个锁着的文件夹等着管理员

branches.en: a gate, whether of wood or of software
branches.cn: 一道门，木头做的或软件做的都一样

intro.en: A Latin prefix of passage, a Latin verb of sending and a noun ending that turns the act into a thing hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示穿过的拉丁前缀、表示送出的拉丁动词，以及把动作变成名词的词尾，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: mittere, permittere and permissio all survive inside English borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族的拉丁词有清楚记录：mittere、permittere、permissio 都通过借词留在了英语里。

definition_zh: 允许；准许；使成为可能；许可证；执照
definition_en: to allow something to happen or someone to do something; also an official document that gives you the right to do something
core_image: 一只手在闸机旁按下按钮，横杆抬起，让一个人走过去
scene: 停车场入口的栏杆旁，管理员把一张塑封卡片放在挡风玻璃后面，示意司机可以开进去了。A resident permit lets you park here all year.
sceneCN: 这里是名词「许可证」（第 4 个义项：官方发放、允许持有人在特定范围内活动的证件）；句意为有了居民停车证，就能整年停在这里。画面里是挡风玻璃后的那张卡。

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁动词 permittere 的动作名词 permissio 演变而来，义为「许可」；与 permit 同源，名词形式不同
由词干 permiss- 加 -ive 构成，义为「宽容的；放任的」
由词干 permiss- 加 -ible 构成，义为「可允许的」

senses.title: To allow someone to do something
senses.definition: to give someone the right to do something, especially through an authority or a rule
senses.definitionCN: 尤指通过权威或规则给予某人做某事的权利
senses.example: The library does not permit food or drink at the desks.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆不允许在桌边吃东西或喝饮料。
senses.why: Latin permittere is per-, through, plus mittere, to let go: the word begins as a physical letting-through and ends as a social yes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 permittere 是 per-（穿过）加 mittere（放开），本义是让某物通过，后来才转成社会意义上的点头同意。

senses.title: To make something possible
senses.definition: to make an action possible, said of conditions such as weather, time or money
senses.definitionCN: 使某个行动成为可能，多就天气、时间、金钱等条件而言
senses.example: The narrow road did not permit two cars to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路太窄，两辆车过不去。
senses.why: If a condition lets an action pass through, the same verb naturally comes to mean that the condition makes the action possible.
senses.whyCN: 如果某个条件让一个动作通过，这个动词自然就表示条件使动作成为可能，这就是从允许到使得以的那一步。

senses.title: To authorize formally, as a body does
senses.definition: to give official approval for an activity, often in writing
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动给予正式批准，常为书面形式
senses.example: The city permitted the closure of two lanes for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 市政部门批准封闭两条车道进行维修。
senses.why: Institutions need a word for the official version of yes and took over the verb that already meant letting through.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个表示官方同意的词，就直接沿用本来表示放行的这个动词，正式批准义由此而来。

senses.title: An official document allowing an activity
senses.definition: an official document that allows you to do something or to go somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 允许你做某事或去某处的正式证件
senses.example: He was stopped at the gate because his permit had expired.
senses.exampleCN: 他在门口被拦下，因为他的许可证过期了。
senses.why: English turned the verb into a countable noun in the nineteenth century, so the permission itself became a piece of paper you carry.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪英语把这个动词转成可数名词，那份允许于是变成一张随身携带的纸，这就是许可证义的来路。

intro.en: Permit comes straight from Latin permittere, to let through; the noun use is a later English reuse of the same form.
intro.cn: permit 直接来自拉丁语 permittere（放行、允许）；名词用法是同一个词形在英语里后起的转用。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to release and supplied the core of many Latin verbs of letting go.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放开，是许多表示放手的拉丁动词的核心。

items.en: Per- added the idea of passage, giving permittere, to let something go through.
items.cn: 加上表示通过的 per-，构成 permittere，意为让某物穿过去。

items.en: The noun permissio grew up beside the verb and named the act of letting through.
items.cn: 名词 permissio 与动词并行发展，用来指放行这件事。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century, at first in legal and official writing.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，最早见于法律与公文。

items.en: The countable noun for a licence appears in the nineteenth century, and compounds such as work permit follow.
items.cn: 表示许可证的可数名词在十九世纪出现，工作许可证一类的复合词随之而来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds relatives of the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group holds verbs and nouns of consent and official leave.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁动词的同族词；近义组收表示同意与官方放行的动词和名词。

entries.definition: The action noun of the same Latin verb; unlike permit, it is almost always uncountable.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁动词的动作名词；与 permit 不同，它几乎总是不可数。

entries.definition: Allowing much freedom and not imposing strict limits.
entries.definitionCN: 给予很大自由、不施加严格限制的。

entries.definition: Allowed by a rule, a law or a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 规则、法律或标准所允许的。

entries.definition: A task given to someone and sent with them, from the Latin verb of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 交给某人并随之前往的任务，出自表示送出的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To let something happen without opposing it, the most general verb of this kind.
entries.definitionCN: 不加以反对地让某事发生，是这类动词中最通用的一个。

entries.definition: To give official power or approval for an action.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项行动给予正式权力或批准。

entries.definition: A document that allows an activity, usually after payment and checks.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某项活动的证件，通常需付费并通过审查。

entries.definition: To allow something, used above all in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某事，主要用于日常口语。

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb of letting through gives both the act of allowing and the card that proves it.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个表示放行的拉丁动词，既给出允许这个动作，也给出证明允许的那张卡。

normal.en: Mittere is to send, so to permit is to send something on its way instead of stopping it.
normal.cn: mittere 是送出，所以 permit 是把事情放它走，而不是把它拦住。

normal.en: The past tense doubles the t: permitted, because the stress rests on the final syllable.
normal.cn: 过去式双写 t 写作 permitted，因为重音压在最后一个音节上。

normal.en: As a verb the stress falls on the second syllable, as a noun it moves to the first.
normal.cn: 作动词时重音在第二音节，作名词时移到第一音节。

normal.en: Weather permitting is a fixed absolute phrase meaning if the weather allows it.
normal.cn: 天气允许的话是固定的独立结构，意思是如果天气条件许可。

normal.en: A work permit, a parking permit and a residence permit are all papers, not acts of allowing.
normal.cn: 工作许可证、停车证、居留许可，说的都是纸面证件，而不是允许这个动作。

abstract.en: A permit is a small rectangle of card standing in for a person's word, so the gate trusts the paper rather than you.
abstract.cn: permit 是一小张纸卡，代替某个人的口头承诺，于是闸机信的是纸，不是你。

abstract.en: To permit is to step aside: the verb describes not doing something, and that is its whole content.
abstract.cn: 允许就是往旁边让一步；这个动词描述的是一种不作为，它的全部内容就在这里。

abstract.en: Every permit carries a boundary, saying how long and how far, which is why a licence can expire.
abstract.cn: 每一张许可证都带着边界，说明多久、多远，所以证件才会过期。

examples.en: Smoking is not permitted anywhere inside the building.
examples.cn: 楼内任何地方都不准吸烟。

examples.en: If the weather permits, we will hold the ceremony outside.
examples.cn: 如果天气允许，我们会在户外举行仪式。

examples.en: Her permit allows her to work in the country for two years.
examples.cn: 她的许可证允许她在这个国家工作两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼米特」——闸机前有人泼了一地米，特批之后才放你过去；permit 就是允许。

root: 拉丁语 permittere（per- 穿过 + mittere 送出）意为放行、允许；名词 permit 是英语后起的转用，与 permission 同源而词形不同。

sensesIntro.en: One Latin verb of letting through supplies both the act of allowing and the paper that proves it.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示放行的拉丁动词，既提供了允许这个动作，也提供了证明允许的那张纸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing the button beside a barrier so that the bar lifts and someone walks through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在闸机旁按下按钮，横杆抬起，让一个人走过去。

branches.en: a barrier lifting for one person
branches.cn: 横杆为一个人抬起

branches.en: a narrow lane where two cars cannot meet
branches.cn: 窄路上两车无法交会

branches.en: a signed order closing two lanes
branches.cn: 一纸批准封闭两条车道的公文

branches.en: a card checked at a gate
branches.cn: 在门口被查验的一张卡

branches.en: the same yes spoken once and printed once
branches.cn: 同一个「可以」，一次说出口，一次印在纸上

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin prefix of passage, a Latin verb of sending, and an English habit of turning verbs into countable nouns.
intro.cn: 这个词靠表示穿过的拉丁前缀、表示送出的拉丁动词，以及英语把动词转成可数名词的习惯支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry is recorded without gaps: mittere, permittere and permissio all survive in English borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: 这一支的拉丁来历有完整记录：mittere、permittere、permissio 都以借词形式留在英语里。

definition_zh: 坚持；持续；执意；存留；持久化
definition_en: to keep doing something despite difficulty, or to continue to exist beyond the expected time
core_image: 一个人站在原地不动，风一直吹，他始终没退一步。
scene: 他退烧之后，咳嗽又持续了三个星期。The cough persisted for three weeks after the fever cleared.
sceneCN: 这里 persist 是「（症状）持续不退」（第 3 个义项：病症延续）；句意：退烧之后，咳嗽还持续了三周。场景要点：药瓶、日历上划掉的日期、仍在咳的人；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 坚持不懈的；持续的；顽固的
非持久的（多用于计算机或化学语境）

senses.title: Keep going despite difficulty
senses.definition: to continue an effort even when it is hard or slow to succeed
senses.definitionCN: 即使困难或见效缓慢，仍继续努力
senses.example: She persisted with the experiment after four failed trials.
senses.exampleCN: 四次试验失败后，她仍坚持做这个实验。
senses.why: Latin sistere meant 'to stand firm, take a stand'. Persist is per- 'thoroughly' + sistere: to stand your ground all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sistere 意为“站稳、站定”。persist 是 per-“彻底”+ sistere：从头到尾站住不退。

senses.title: Continue to exist
senses.definition: of a condition, practice, or thing, to continue to exist over time
senses.definitionCN: 指某种状况、做法或事物随时间继续存在
senses.example: The custom persists in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在农村地区仍然存在。
senses.why: The standing image is applied to existence itself: something that stands does not fall away, so it keeps being there.
senses.whyCN: “站住”的意象被用在存在本身：站住的东西不会倒掉，因此一直还在。

senses.title: Of a symptom: fail to clear
senses.definition: of an illness or symptom, to continue longer than expected
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或症状持续的时间超过预期
senses.example: See a doctor if the fever persists for more than three days.
senses.exampleCN: 如果发烧持续超过三天，请就医。
senses.why: A symptom is something standing in the body that refuses to leave. The verb marks duration, not effort, which is why medical usage is so common.
senses.whyCN: 症状是站在身体里不肯走的东西。这个动词标记的是“时程”而非“努力”，所以医学用法很常见。

senses.title: Of a smell or trace: remain
senses.definition: of a smell, taste, impression, or mark, to remain after its source has gone
senses.definitionCN: 指气味、味道、印象或痕迹在来源消失后仍然留着
senses.example: The smell of smoke persisted in the curtains for days.
senses.exampleCN: 烟味在窗帘上留了好几天。
senses.why: The trace keeps standing in the material even after the fire is out. Persistence here is physical stubbornness.
senses.whyCN: 火灭了，痕迹仍站在布料里。这里的持续，是一种物理上的不肯走。

senses.title: Keep asking or doing, annoyingly
senses.definition: to continue doing or asking something in a way that others find hard to stop
senses.definitionCN: 以别人难以阻止的方式反复做或反复问
senses.example: He persisted in calling until she answered.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直打个不停，直到她接电话。
senses.why: The same standing firm can be read from outside as refusal to take no for an answer. The virtue turns into a nuisance.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“站住”，从外面看就是不肯接受“不”。美德由此变成了烦扰。

senses.title: Of a belief or institution: survive
senses.titleCN: 观念延续：穿过年代还在
senses.definition: of a belief, institution, or idea, to survive over a long time
senses.definitionCN: 指信念、制度或观念长期存续下来
senses.example: The belief persisted long after the empire fell.
senses.exampleCN: 帝国灭亡很久之后，这种信仰仍然延续。
senses.why: Institutions stand longer than the people who hold them up. Persistence becomes a measure of historical survival.
senses.whyCN: 制度比撑着它的人站得更久。持续由此成为衡量历史存活的尺度。

senses.title: Computing: store data permanently
senses.definition: of data, to remain stored after a program or device stops running
senses.definitionCN: 指数据在程序或设备停止运行后仍然保留
senses.example: The settings persist even after a restart.
senses.exampleCN: 即使重启，设置也会保留。
senses.why: Memory that vanishes is data that could not stand. Persistent storage is the technical version of 'still standing after the power goes off'.
senses.whyCN: 一断电就消失的记忆，是站不住的数据。持久化存储，就是“断电后仍站着”的技术版本。

senses.title: Insist stubbornly against advice
senses.definition: to continue in a course of action in spite of warnings or good advice
senses.definitionCN: 不顾警告或善意劝告，继续照自己的做法行事
senses.example: He persisted in driving despite the closed-road signs.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管有封路标志，他仍执意开车。
senses.why: Standing firm with no reason to stand is stubbornness. The word does not judge by itself; the context decides whether to praise or blame.
senses.whyCN: 没有理由还站着，就是固执。这个词本身不作评判，是语境决定该夸还是该责。

intro.en: Persist is Latin per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'to stand firm', from the same Indo-European root as stand. The core is not effort but posture: staying on your feet.
intro.cn: persist 是拉丁语 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站稳”，与 stand 同出一个印欧词根。它的核心不是努力，而是姿态：站住不倒。

items.en: The root *sta- gives Latin stare 'to stand', sistere 'cause to stand', and English stand, stable, statue, and constant.
items.cn: 词根 *sta- 衍生出拉丁语 stare“站”、sistere“使站住”，以及英语 stand、stable、statue、constant。

items.en: Sistere meant 'to cause to stand, place, stop'. Its frequentative form was used for holding a position, which is the seed of 'persist'.
items.cn: sistere 意为“使站住、安置、停住”。它的反复形式用于“守住位置”，这正是 persist 的种子。

items.en: Persistere combined per- 'through, thoroughly' with sistere: 'to continue standing, persevere, persist'.
items.cn: persistere 把 per-“贯穿、彻底”与 sistere 结合：“一直站住、坚持、持续”。

items.en: English records persist in the 1530s, first of persons continuing in a course, then of things continuing to exist.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 30 年代记录 persist，先指人继续走某条路，后指事物继续存在。

items.en: The medical sense of a symptom that will not clear and the physical sense of a smell that remains both grow from the same 'still standing' image.
items.cn: 症状不退的医学义与气味残留的物理义，都从同一个“仍站着”的意象长出来。

items.en: Persistent storage and persistent data apply the old verb to memory that survives a restart. Persistence becomes a technical property.
items.cn: persistent storage 与 persistent data 把这个老动词用在重启后仍存活的内存上。持续由此成为一种技术属性。

note.en: The first group is the persist family plus the Latin verb behind it; the second separates near-synonyms by what exactly keeps going.
note.cn: 第一组是 persist 词族及其背后的拉丁动词；第二组按“究竟是什么在继续”区分近义词。

entries.definition: the quality of continuing despite difficulty, or of lasting. It is the noun of persist.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管困难仍继续的品质，或持久性。它是 persist 的名词。

entries.definition: continuing firmly or lasting a long time. It describes the person or thing, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持不懈的；持续时间长的。它描述人或物，而非动作。

entries.definition: a rarer synonym of persistence, used especially in older technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: persistence 的较罕见同义词，多用于较早的技术文献。

entries.definition: not lasting, used of chemicals that break down quickly and of network connections that close after use.
entries.definitionCN: 不持久的，用于快速降解的化学品，或用完即关闭的网络连接。

entries.definition: to keep trying despite difficulty. It is close to persist but almost always about deliberate human effort toward a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管困难仍不断尝试。它与 persist 接近，但几乎总指人为目标付出的努力。

entries.definition: to keep happening or doing without stopping. It is the neutral word and carries no idea of resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 不停地继续发生或做。它最中性，不含抵抗之意。

entries.definition: to suffer something difficult patiently, or to last a long time. It adds the weight of suffering or durability.
entries.definitionCN: 耐心承受艰难，或长久存在。它加了受苦或耐久的分量。

entries.definition: to stay longer than expected, often unwillingly. It is used of smells, illness, and people who should go.
entries.definitionCN: 比预期停留更久，常含不愿离开。它用于气味、疾病与该走的人。

entries.definition: to demand something firmly. It is about a claim or demand, while persist is about continuing an action.
entries.definitionCN: 坚决要求。它关于主张或要求，而 persist 关于继续行动。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'stand firm', from PIE *sta- 'stand'. Family words persistence, persistent, persistently; relatives stand, stable, statue, constant.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站稳”，源自原始印欧语 *sta-“站”。词族为 persistence、persistent、persistently；亲属词 stand、stable、statue、constant。

normal.en: Sistere is 'stand firm'; persist is standing firm all the way through.
normal.cn: sistere 是“站稳”；persist 就是从头到尾一直站稳。

normal.en: Stand, stable, statue, constant, persist: one *sta- family of standing.
normal.cn: stand、stable、statue、constant、persist：同一个 *sta-“站立”家族。

normal.en: A persistent cough is a cough that will not stand down.
normal.cn: persistent cough 就是不肯“退下”的咳嗽。

normal.en: Persistent data is data still standing after the power is cut.
normal.cn: persistent data 就是断电后仍站着的数据。

normal.en: Persist in and persist with are both about refusing to leave the spot.
normal.cn: persist in 与 persist with，都是不肯离开那个位置。

abstract.en: Persistence is often just the decision to remain where the difficulty is.
abstract.cn: 坚持，常常只是决定留在困难所在的那个地方。

abstract.en: What persists shapes the world more than what is intense.
abstract.cn: 留下来的东西，比强烈的东西更能塑造世界。

abstract.en: To persist is to make time your ally rather than your judge.
abstract.cn: 坚持，就是把时间变成盟友，而不是法官。

examples.en: The team persisted through two years of rejected applications.
examples.cn: 团队在两年申请被拒的情况下仍坚持下来。

examples.en: Old farming methods persist in the valley.
examples.cn: 古老的耕作方式在山谷里仍然延续。

examples.en: The rash persisted after the course of antibiotics ended.
examples.cn: 抗生素疗程结束后，皮疹仍未消退。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破吸石”——破吸盘还能吸在石头上不掉，风再大也不松 → persist 坚持、持续

root: 源自拉丁语 persistere“一直站住、坚持”，由 per-“贯穿、彻底”+ sistere“站稳、使站住”构成；sistere 与 stare“站”同出原始印欧语 *sta-“站”，故与 stand、stable、statue、constant 同源。核心是“站住不倒”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of persist, all one posture: something stays standing when it could have fallen, stopped, or gone away.
sensesIntro.cn: persist 的八个义项是同一个姿态：本可以倒下、停止或离开的东西，仍然站着。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing in wind, feet planted, not moving back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在风里，双脚钉住，不退一步。

branches.en: WILL: effort and stubbornness are the same posture seen from inside and from outside.
branches.cn: 意志：努力与固执，是同一个姿态从里面和外面看的样子。

branches.en: EXISTENCE: a custom or belief stands longer than the people holding it up.
branches.cn: 存在：习俗或信仰，比撑着它的人站得更久。

branches.en: TRACES: a symptom and a smell both stay in the body or the cloth after their cause is gone.
branches.cn: 痕迹：症状与气味，都在成因消失后仍留在身体或布料里。

branches.en: PRESSURE: asking again and again is standing firm in someone else's doorway.
branches.cn: 压力：一遍遍追问，就是在别人的门口站住不走。

branches.en: MACHINES: persistent storage is memory that survives the power being switched off.
branches.cn: 机器：持久化存储，是断电后仍存活的内存。

intro.en: Persist's family is built on Latin sistere 'to stand firm'. Suffixes mark the state, the person or thing, and the manner; non- removes the lasting.
intro.cn: persist 的词族建立在拉丁语 sistere“站稳”上。后缀标记状态、人与方式；non- 则取消“持久”。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are stare 'to stand', sistere 'cause to stand', and persistere 'continue standing'. The whole family belongs to PIE *sta-.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是 stare“站”、sistere“使站住”与 persistere“继续站住”。整个词族都属于原始印欧语 *sta-。

items.meaning: the fact or quality of continuing or lasting
items.meaningCN: 继续或持久的事实或品质（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: Her persistence eventually won the funding.
items.exampleCN: 她的坚持最终争取到了资助。

items.meaning: continuing firmly or lasting a long time
items.meaningCN: 坚持不懈的；持续时间长的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 持续不断的雨取消了比赛。

items.meaning: in a continuing or stubborn manner
items.meaningCN: 持续地；固执地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: a rarer form of persistence, chiefly technical
items.meaningCN: persistence 的较罕见形式，主要用于技术文献
items.example: The persistency of the pesticide was measured in soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种农药在土壤中的持久性被测定了。

items.meaning: not lasting long in the environment or in memory
items.meaningCN: 在环境中或内存中不长久留存的（non- 表示否定）
items.example: Non-persistent chemicals break down within weeks.
items.exampleCN: 非持久性化学品在几周内降解。

items.meaning: to continue doing something, often against advice
items.meaningCN: 继续做某事，常指不听劝（in 标记活动）
items.example: They persisted in asking for a written answer.
items.exampleCN: 他们执意要求一份书面答复。

items.meaning: to continue with a task or plan
items.meaningCN: 继续某项工作或计划（with 标记对象）
items.example: She persisted with the treatment for a full year.
items.exampleCN: 她坚持治疗了整整一年。

items.meaning: a person who keeps committing offences
items.meaningCN: 反复犯罪的人（法律术语）
items.example: He was classified as a persistent offender.

items.meaning: memory that keeps data after power is removed
items.meaningCN: 断电后仍保存数据的存储（计算机术语）
items.example: The logs are written to persistent storage.
items.exampleCN: 日志被写入持久化存储。

items.meaning: the way an image stays on the retina briefly and makes film appear to move
items.meaningCN: 图像在视网膜上短暂停留、使电影看起来在动的现象
items.example: Animation relies on the persistence of vision.

latinEntries.meaning: to cause to stand, place, stop

definition_zh: 个人的；私人的；亲自的；涉及私生活的；人称的
definition_en: relating to one particular person rather than to others, or done by that person directly
core_image: 一只抽屉拉开一道缝，里面是只属于一个人的旧照片、钥匙和一封没寄出的信
scene: 搬家那天，纸箱上写着同一个名字，里面装着相册、旧信和一只用了多年的杯子，都是不打算与人分享的东西。She keeps her personal letters in a locked drawer.
sceneCN: 这里是「个人的、私人的」（第 1 个义项：属于某一个人而非公共的）；句意为她把私人信件锁在抽屉里。画面里那只抽屉只为一个名字打开。

pos.zh: 个人的；私人的；亲自的；人称的

derivatives.zh: 由 personal 加 -ly 构成，义为「亲自；就个人而言」
由同一词干改接 -ity 构成，义为「性格；人格」
拉丁语 persona 经古法语进入英语，义为「人；个人」
由否定前缀 im- 加 personal 构成，义为「非个人的；没有人情味的」
由 personal 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使个性化」

senses.title: Belonging to one person alone
senses.definition: belonging to or used by one particular person and not shared with others
senses.definitionCN: 属于或供某一个特定的人使用，不与别人共有
senses.example: Please keep your personal papers in this folder.
senses.exampleCN: 请把你的私人文件放在这个文件夹里。
senses.why: The word starts from Latin persona, the mask that marked one character on stage, so anything personal is tied to a single someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从拉丁语 persona 出发，那是舞台上一个角色所戴的面具，因此凡是 personal 的东西都系在某一个具体的人身上。

senses.title: Done by the person himself or herself
senses.definition: done by the person directly rather than through someone else
senses.definitionCN: 由本人直接去做，而不是经由别人
senses.example: The director paid a personal visit to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 主任亲自上门探望了这家人。
senses.why: If something belongs to one person, it can also be what that person does with his own hands instead of sending a stand-in.
senses.whyCN: 既然某样东西可以专属一个人，也就可以指这个人亲手去做、不派代表的事，亲自义正是从所属义挪过来的。

senses.title: Concerning private feelings or private life
senses.titleCN: 涉及私生活的；针对个人的
senses.definition: touching on someone's private life or feelings, often in a way that feels intrusive
senses.definitionCN: 触及某人的私生活或感情，常带冒犯、探究的意味
senses.example: The reporter asked a personal question about her marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 记者问了一个涉及她婚姻的私人问题。
senses.why: Once the word marks the area that belongs to one person, a question entering that area is felt as a crossing of the line.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先划出属于一个人的地盘，问题一旦踏进这块地盘，就被感受为越界，于是带上冒犯、探私的色彩。

senses.title: Showing grammatical person
senses.definition: used in grammar for forms that show whether the speaker, the listener or a third party is meant
senses.definitionCN: 语法中用来表明所指的是说话人、听话人还是第三方的形式
senses.example: In English the personal pronouns change form between subject and object.
senses.exampleCN: 英语的人称代词在主格和宾格之间会变形。
senses.why: Grammarians needed a label for the forms that shift with who is speaking, and persona already meant the role a speaker takes.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家需要给随说话人而变的词形起个名字，而 persona 本来就有「所扮演的角色」之意，正好拿来用。

intro.en: Personal comes from Latin persona, a mask and the role worn with it; the adjective personalis was built on that noun and reached English through French.
intro.cn: personal 来自拉丁语 persona，指面具以及随面具而来的角色；形容词 personalis 由这个名词构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Persona named the mask an actor wore and, by extension, the character played; its earlier origin is uncertain and may be Etruscan.
items.cn: persona 指演员戴的面具，进而指所扮演的角色；它更早的来源不确定，可能与伊特鲁里亚语有关。

items.en: Late Latin formed personalis, meaning of a person, on the noun persona.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语在 persona 之上构成 personalis，意为属于某个人的。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective as personel, still close to the sense of belonging to a particular person.
items.cn: 古法语以 personel 的形式使用这个形容词，仍保留属于某个特定人的意思。

items.en: Middle English personal appears in the fourteenth century, first in legal and religious writing about the rights of one person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 personal 出现在十四世纪，最早见于讨论个人权利的法律与宗教文献。

items.en: Modern English extends it to privacy, to doing something oneself, and to grammar, where it labels the pronouns of speaker and listener.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到隐私、亲自做事，以及语法中标记说话人与听话人的代词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin noun for a mask and a role; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of what belongs to one person.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在表示面具与角色的拉丁名词上的词；近义组收表示属于某一个人的形容词。

entries.definition: A single human being, the noun from which the adjective was built.
entries.definitionCN: 一个单独的人，是构成这个形容词的名词。

entries.definition: The set of qualities that make a person distinctive.
entries.definitionCN: 使一个人与众不同的那组特质。

entries.definition: The adverb built on the adjective, meaning in one's own body or in one's own view.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个形容词构成的副词，意为亲自或就本人看来。

entries.definition: Without human warmth, or without reference to any particular person.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏人情味，或不指向任何具体的人。

entries.definition: Belonging to one person and kept from public view.
entries.definitionCN: 属于一个人、不向公众公开的。

entries.definition: Relating to one single person, seen apart from the group.
entries.definitionCN: 与单个的人有关、被从群体中单独看待的。

entries.definition: Used to stress that something belongs to the person just mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 用来强调某物属于刚提到的那个人。

entries.definition: Very close and private, said of feelings and relationships.
entries.definitionCN: 形容感情与关系时指非常亲密而私密的。

normalIntro.en: A Latin mask, a Latin adjective ending and two English suffixes carry the idea of one person from the stage to grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语的面具、一个拉丁语形容词词尾和两个英语后缀，把一个人的念头从舞台一路带到语法。

normal.en: Persona was a stage mask, so personal still carries the sense of one particular face rather than a crowd.
normal.cn: persona 本是舞台面具，所以 personal 至今带着某一张具体的脸、而不是一群人的意味。

normal.en: Person is the noun, personal the adjective, personally the adverb: one meaning in three jobs.
normal.cn: person 是名词，personal 是形容词，personally 是副词：一个意思，三种岗位。

normal.en: Impersonal adds the negative prefix and takes the human warmth away.
normal.cn: impersonal 加上否定前缀，就把人情味拿走了。

normal.en: A personal pronoun is the one place where grammar openly asks who is speaking.
normal.cn: 人称代词正是语法公开追问谁在说话的地方。

normal.en: Personal belongings and private belongings overlap, but personal stresses the owner while private stresses the closed door.
normal.cn: 个人物品与私人物品意思相近，但 personal 强调归属，private 强调关起来不让人看。

abstract.en: A mask that becomes a person: the word itself shows how a role hardens into an identity.
abstract.cn: 从面具变成人：这个词的来历本身就说明一个角色如何凝固成一个身份。

abstract.en: Personal is a line drawn around one body; whatever is inside the line may be shared, but only by permission.
abstract.cn: personal 是在一具身体周围画下的线；线内的一切都可以分享，但必须经过允许。

abstract.en: When a rule is called impersonal, it is being blamed for not seeing the faces it applies to.
abstract.cn: 当一条规则被说成没有人情味，其实是在责怪它看不见自己所管辖的那些脸。

examples.en: She packed her personal belongings into two boxes.
examples.cn: 她把个人物品装进两个箱子。

examples.en: He never discusses his personal life with colleagues.
examples.cn: 他从不与同事谈论自己的私生活。

examples.en: This is a personal letter, not a public statement.
examples.cn: 这是一封私人信件，不是公开声明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼森呢」——下雨天只有一把破伞，撑开也只够护住自己一个人；personal 就是个人的、私人的。

root: 拉丁语 persona（面具、角色，更早来源不确定）构成晚期拉丁语 personalis，经古法语 personel 进入英语；同族词多与人、身份有关。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with one person and spreads outward: what that person owns, what that person does, what is private, and finally who is speaking in a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一个「人」出发向外扩：属于这个人的东西、这个人亲自做的事、只属于他的私密领域，最后是句子里标明谁在说话的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawer pulled open a little, showing a photograph, a key and a letter that belong to one person only.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只抽屉拉开一道缝，里面是只属于一个人的旧照片、钥匙和一封没寄出的信。

branches.en: a drawer with a name written inside the lid
branches.cn: 抽屉盖内侧写着一个名字

branches.en: a director standing at a doorstep himself
branches.cn: 主任自己站到了门口

branches.en: a question that makes the room go quiet
branches.cn: 一个让全场安静下来的问题

branches.en: a pronoun pointing back at the speaker
branches.cn: 一个代词指回说话人

branches.en: things that belong to you and things you do yourself
branches.cn: 属于你的东西与你亲自做的事

intro.en: A Latin mask, a Latin adjective ending and two English suffixes let one word name a person, a private thing and a grammatical role.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语面具、一个拉丁语形容词词尾和两个英语后缀，让同一个词既能指人、又能指私人之物，还能指语法角色。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is recorded as persona and personalis; the earlier origin of persona itself remains uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源可查为 persona 与 personalis；不过 persona 更早的出处并不确定。

definition_zh: 个性；性格；人格；名人；魅力；地方或事物的鲜明风格
definition_en: the whole pattern of qualities that makes a person distinct, or a famous person, or the quality of being vividly oneself
core_image: 同一张素坯在窑里被反复上釉，最后开窑时只有它一只带着那种说不出名字的亮
scene: 面试官问了他三个问题，最后只记下一句：这个人说话时会停下来听别人说完。The interviewer noted a personality that made the room slow down.
sceneCN: 这里 personality 指「一个人整体上给人的性格印象」（第 1 个义项：整体的性格格局）；句意是面试官注意到一种让整个房间放慢下来的性格。图中可辨识物件：面试桌、停在半空的笔、两份摊开的简历；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 名人（尤指娱乐界、媒体人物）

derivatives.zh: 使失去个性；使非人格化

senses.title: The whole pattern of a person
senses.titleCN: 一个人整体的性格格局
senses.definition: the total set of qualities that makes one person different from another
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人区别于另一个人的全部品质所构成的整体
senses.example: The interviewer noted a personality that made the room slow down.
senses.exampleCN: 面试官注意到一种让整个房间放慢下来的性格。
senses.why: the word was built from the name for a mask, so it names the face a person presents to the world in all its parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「面具」一词构成，因此命名的是一个人向世界呈现的整张脸，连同它的各个部分。

senses.title: An object of psychological study
senses.definition: the measurable structure of traits that psychologists describe and classify
senses.definitionCN: 心理学家加以描述与分类的那些可测量的特质结构
senses.example: The field treats personality as a set of dimensions rather than a single score.
senses.exampleCN: 这个领域把人格当作一组维度，而不是一个单一分数。
senses.why: once qualities are counted and rated, the whole pattern becomes a research object with its own instruments.
senses.whyCN: 品质一旦被计数与评级，整个格局就成了一个有自己仪器配套的研究对象。

senses.title: A famous face
senses.definition: a well-known person, especially one who appears in media
senses.definitionCN: 广为人知的人，尤指常在媒体露面者
senses.example: A television personality opened the charity event.
senses.exampleCN: 一位电视名人主持了这场慈善活动。
senses.why: public life reduces a whole person to the face the public knows, so the word slides from the pattern to the person who carries it.
senses.whyCN: 公众生活把整个人压缩成公众认得的那张脸，于是词义从格局滑向承载它的那个人。

senses.title: Charm that fills a room
senses.titleCN: 能撑起一间屋子的魅力
senses.definition: a quality of presence that draws attention and holds it
senses.definitionCN: 一种让人注意并被吸住的存在感
senses.example: The old hostess had more personality than the whole cast.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老女主人比整台演员加起来更有魅力。
senses.why: when the pattern is vivid enough, it stops being a description and becomes an effect on others.
senses.whyCN: 当这个格局鲜明到一定程度，它就不再是描述，而成了对他人产生的效果。

senses.title: A place with a face of its own
senses.definition: the distinctive character of a building, street or brand
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、街道或品牌所带的鲜明性格
senses.example: The market kept its personality even after the renovation.
senses.exampleCN: 改造之后这个市场仍保有自己的性格。
senses.why: the metaphor is easy to move outward: whatever presents a consistent face to people can be said to have a personality.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很容易向外搬：凡是向人呈现一致面孔的东西，都可以说有性格。

senses.title: A classified type
senses.definition: one of the recognised kinds into which patterns of character are sorted
senses.definitionCN: 把性格格局分门别类之后得到的某一类
senses.example: The test sorts people into four personality types.
senses.exampleCN: 这个测验把人分成四种人格类型。
senses.why: classification is the next step after measurement, and the noun then serves as the label of a class.
senses.whyCN: 测量之后的下一步是分类，这个名词于是充当某一类的标签。

senses.title: Friction between two patterns
senses.definition: the incompatibility that arises when two people's habits of behaviour do not fit
senses.definitionCN: 两个人的行为习惯合不来时产生的不相容
senses.example: The project failed on a personality clash, not on the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 项目败于性格冲突，而不是预算。
senses.why: the word can name a cause of trouble, which shows how much weight English gives to the pattern itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以命名麻烦的起因，可见英语把这个格局本身看得多重。

senses.title: Legal standing as a person
senses.definition: the status of being recognised as a person before the law, as held by a company
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上被认作人的地位，公司也可具有
senses.example: A company has legal personality separate from its owners.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在法律上具有独立于其所有者的人格。
senses.why: the oldest layer of the word is the mask that a role makes one wear, and law still speaks of the mask a body wears.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是角色所戴的面具，法律至今仍在说某个实体所戴的那张面具。

intro.en: Personality comes from Latin personalitas, built on persona 'a mask, a character in a play'. The origin of persona itself is not established; the old explanation that it meant 'something through which sound passes' is a hypothesis. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: personality 来自拉丁 personalitas，由 persona「面具、剧中角色」构成。persona 本身的来源未得到证明；旧说认为它指「声音从中穿过之物」，那只是假说。年代均为约数。

items.en: Persona named a mask worn by an actor and, by extension, the role played. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a link to a borrowed Etruscan word is one hypothesis among several.
items.cn: persona 指演员戴的面具，引申为所演的角色。其更深来源不确定；认为它借自某种伊特鲁里亚词，只是若干假说之一。

items.en: The abstract noun named the quality of being a particular person, first in legal and theological writing about the status of an individual.
items.cn: 这个抽象名词指「作为某个特定个人的性质」，最早见于讨论个人地位的法律与神学文字。

items.en: English took the word in the eighteenth century for the sum of a person's qualities, at a time when portraits and novels were making individuality interesting.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪借入这个词，指一个人品质的总和，当时肖像画与小说正让「个体性」变得有趣。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century psychology turned it into a measurable structure, giving rise to tests, types and disorders.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪心理学把它变成可测量的结构，于是有了测验、类型与障碍。

items.en: Twentieth-century broadcasting made the word mean a famous face as well as an inner pattern, and the two senses now coexist.
items.cn: 20 世纪的广播电视让这个词既指有名的面孔，也指内在格局，两个义项如今并存。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of persona is a reconstruction, and the exact first English use of the abstract noun is not agreed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：persona 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，这个抽象名词在英语中最早的确切用例也无公认结论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Latin word for a mask, whose meanings have drifted apart; group two holds the character words that overlap with this one.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「面具」一词、意义却已分流的词；第二组是与本词重叠的性格类词。

entries.definition: The plain noun for an individual human being; this word names the pattern that individual carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个的人的普通名词；本词命名的是那个人所带的格局。

entries.definition: Said of things that belong to or concern one individual, such as a personal letter; it never means 'full of character'.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于或涉及某一个人的东西，如私人信件；从不表示「有性格」。

entries.definition: Describes someone easy to like on first meeting, which is a social impression rather than a whole pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 形容初次见面就容易让人喜欢，是社会印象，而非整体格局。

entries.definition: The borrowed Latin word for the face one presents in public, often deliberately different from the private self.
entries.definitionCN: 借来的拉丁词，指在公众面前呈现的那张脸，常刻意与私下自我不同。

entries.definition: Overlaps in the sense of make-up, but character also judges moral fibre, which personality does not.
entries.definitionCN: 在「构成」这一义上重叠，但 character 还评判道德骨气，而 personality 不作此评判。

entries.definition: The part of the pattern thought to be native and steady; personality includes what experience adds.
entries.definitionCN: 格局中被认为天生而稳定的那部分；personality 还包括经验添上的部分。

entries.definition: The sense of who one is, including group membership; it answers 'who', while this word answers 'what kind'.
entries.definitionCN: 指「我是谁」的认知，包括群体归属；它回答「谁」，而本词回答「什么样」。

entries.definition: A technical term for the self as it mediates; it belongs to theory rather than to everyday description.
entries.definitionCN: 指起中介作用的自我，是理论术语，而非日常描述。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base is Latin persona 'mask', so personality is the face a person wears in all its parts.
normal.cn: 词基是拉丁 persona「面具」，因此 personality 就是一个人戴着的那张完整的脸。

normal.en: The family runs person, personal, personality, personable, impersonate, depersonalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 person、personal、personality、personable、impersonate、depersonalize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: personality traits, personality test, personality clash, television personality.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：人格特质、人格测验、性格冲突、电视名人。

normal.en: Psychologists speak of personality disorders, which shows the technical sense is a whole structure.
normal.cn: 心理学家谈人格障碍，可见专业义指的是整套结构。

normal.en: Law speaks of legal personality, keeping the oldest mask metaphor alive.
normal.cn: 法律说法律人格，让最古老的面具比喻继续活着。

abstract.en: Picture one plain bowl that takes glaze after glaze until only it shines that way.
abstract.cn: 想象一只素坯一遍遍上釉，最后只有它那样发亮。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose furniture rearranges itself around one guest.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子的家具围着一位客人重新排列。

abstract.en: Picture a signature that can be read from across the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一个隔一条街都能认出的签名。

examples.en: The job needs a strong personality and a thick skin.
examples.cn: 这份工作需要强势的性格和厚脸皮。

examples.en: Their personalities never meshed, though their skills did.
examples.cn: 他们的性格始终合不来，技能却互补。

examples.en: The magazine turned a shy researcher into a media personality.
examples.cn: 这家杂志把一位腼腆的研究者变成了媒体名人。

dict_mnemonic.text: person（人）+ ality（性质）——一个人整体的那种性质 → 个性、人格

root: 拉丁 personalitas，由 persona「面具、剧中角色」构成；persona 的更深来源不确定，借自伊特鲁里亚语之说仅为假说之一。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a mask is worn, and that mask is then read as a whole pattern, as something measured, as a famous face, as charm, as the face of a place, as a type, as a cause of friction and finally as legal standing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：一张面具被戴上，这张面具依次被读作整体格局、被测量的对象、有名的面孔、魅力、一个地方的脸、一种类型、摩擦的起因，最后是法律地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one plain bowl that takes glaze after glaze until it alone shines in that particular way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只素坯一遍遍上釉，最后只有它那样发亮。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND ITS INSTRUMENTS: first the whole make-up, then the same make-up turned into dimensions and scores.
branches.cn: 格局与它的仪器：先是整体构成，再是同一构成被变成维度与分数。

branches.en: THE FACE AND ITS FORCE: a famous face is the pattern reduced to what the public sees, and charm is that pattern acting on a room.
branches.cn: 面孔与它的力：名人的脸是被压缩成公众所见之物的格局，魅力则是这格局在一间屋子里起作用。

branches.en: THE SAME FACE ON THINGS: buildings, streets and brands are read as wearing a consistent face.
branches.cn: 同样的脸长在物上：建筑、街道与品牌被读作戴着一张一致的脸。

branches.en: FROM TYPE TO FRICTION: classification gives classes, and putting two classes in one room gives trouble.
branches.cn: 从类型到摩擦：分类给出类别，把两个类别放进同一间屋子就生出麻烦。

branches.en: THE MASK BEFORE THE LAW: legal standing keeps the oldest sense, where a mask makes a thing count as a person.
branches.cn: 法律面前的面具：法律地位保留了最古老的义项，面具使某物被算作人。

intro.en: The word is a Latin abstract noun built on the Latin word for a mask, so the whole family reads from that single image.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁抽象名词，建在拉丁「面具」一词上，因此整个词族都从那张面具读起。

latinIntro.en: Latin persona gives person, personal, personality, personable, persona and impersonate, all through the image of a mask and a role.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 persona 衍生 person、personal、personality、personable、persona、impersonate，全部经由面具与角色的意象。

items.example: The mask is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 那张面具是整个词族的根。

items.example: It produced the adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 它造出表归属的形容词。

items.example: It turned the adjective into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.meaning: the quality of being a particular person
items.meaningCN: 作为某个特定个人的性质
items.exampleCN: 面试官注意到一种性格。
那位候选人很讨人喜欢。
这些表格让申请人失去个人面目。

items.example: Every person wears a mask somewhere.
items.exampleCN: 每个人都在某处戴着面具。

latinEntries.meaning: the quality of being a person

definition_zh: 全体员工；人事部门；（军队或机构的）人员；某类专业人员
definition_en: the people who work for an organization, or the department that manages them; also the members of a force or of a particular group of workers
core_image: 一整面挂满名牌的墙，每块名牌后面都有一个正在上班的人
scene: 清晨的办公楼里，打卡机一声声响起，走廊尽头的人事办公室门口已经排起了队。The personnel files were moved to the third floor last week.
sceneCN: 这里 personnel 指「人事部门」（第 2 个义项：管理员工档案与招聘的部门）；句意为上周人事档案被搬到了三层。图中可辨识物件：打卡机、走廊、写着「人事」的门牌。

pos.zh: 全体员工；人事部门；人员

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 persona（面具、角色）而来，义为「人；个人」
由 person 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「个人的；私人的」
由 personal 加 -ity 构成，义为「个性；人格」
由 personal 加 -ly 构成，义为「亲自；就个人而言」

senses.title: All the people who work for an organization
senses.definition: the whole body of people employed by a company, school, or other organization, considered as one group
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于公司、学校或其他机构的全体人员，被当作一个整体来看
senses.example: The company doubled its personnel within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在一年之内把员工人数翻了一倍。
senses.why: The word entered English as the noun use of a French adjective meaning personal, so it named the persons attached to an organization before it named any office or list.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时，是法语中意为「个人的」那个形容词直接当名词用，所以它先指「挂靠在一个机构下的那些人」，而不是先指某个办公室或名册。

senses.title: The department that hires staff and keeps their records
senses.definition: the office in an organization that deals with hiring, records, and the terms of employment
senses.definitionCN: 机构中负责招聘、档案与雇佣条件的部门
senses.example: She works in personnel at the head office.
senses.exampleCN: 她在总部的人事部门工作。
senses.why: Because personnel already meant the people themselves, the office that counts and files those people took the same name by metonymy, the container named after what it contains.
senses.whyCN: 既然 personnel 已经指人本身，负责清点、归档这些人的办公室就借用了同一个名字，这是以「所管之物」代指「管理机构」的转喻。

senses.title: The members of an armed force, counted as a body
senses.definition: the members of a military force or unit, especially when they are counted or listed
senses.definitionCN: 军队或部队的成员，尤指被清点、列入名册时
senses.example: The wounded personnel were flown out at night.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤人员夜间被空运撤离。
senses.why: Military paperwork treats soldiers as entries on a roll, so personnel in this sense means the names on the list rather than any single soldier.
senses.whyCN: 军队的文书把士兵当成名册上的一条记录，所以这个义项里的 personnel 指名单上的那些人，而不指某一个士兵。

senses.title: People of one particular kind working in an operation
senses.definition: the people of a specified profession or role who are present in a place or taking part in an activity
senses.definitionCN: 某一行业或某一职责的人，出现在某个场所或参与某项行动
senses.example: Medical personnel arrived within ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 医疗人员在十分钟内赶到。
senses.why: The collective frame survives even when the group is defined by a profession, so personnel can attach to a type of worker rather than to a single employer.
senses.whyCN: 即使这群人是由职业来界定的，那个「集体」的框架依然保留，所以 personnel 可以挂在一类工作者身上，而不必依附于某一个雇主。

intro.en: Personnel is a French adjective that became a noun: it began as the personal and ended up meaning the persons.
intro.cn: personnel 本是法语里的一个形容词，后来转成名词：起点是「个人的」，终点是「那些人」。

items.en: Persona first meant a mask worn by an actor, then the role played, and finally the individual who plays it.
items.cn: persona 最初指演员戴的面具，接着指所扮演的角色，最后指扮演角色的那个人。

items.en: The adjective personalis was built on persona and meant belonging to a person.
items.cn: 形容词 personalis 由 persona 构成，意为「属于某个人的」。

items.en: Old French used personel for what belongs to one person, and this form reached English as personal.
items.cn: 古法语用 personel 表示「属于个人的」，这一形式进入英语后成为 personal。

items.en: French turned its adjective personnel into a noun for the staff of an office, and English borrowed that noun in the early nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语把自己的形容词 personnel 转为名词，指一个机关的全班人员；英语在十九世纪初借来了这个名词。

items.en: English kept the French -el spelling, added the human-resources sense in the twentieth century, and still treats the word as a collective with no ordinary singular.
items.cn: 英语保留了法语 -el 的拼法，二十世纪又添上「人事部门」这一义项，并且至今把它当作集合名词，没有日常的单数形式。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin persona through French and English; the near-meaning group gathers words for the people who work somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语 persona 经法语到英语的线索排列；近义组收表示「在某处工作的人」的词。

entries.definition: A single human being, seen as an individual.
entries.definitionCN: 单个的人，作为一个个体来看。

entries.definition: Belonging to or concerning one particular person.
entries.definitionCN: 属于或关于某一个特定的人的。

entries.definition: The set of qualities that make someone who they are.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某人之为某人的那套性格特质。

entries.definition: To pretend to be another person, often to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 假装成另一个人，常带有欺骗目的。

entries.definition: The people who work for a particular organization, treated as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 为某一机构工作的全体人员，作为整体看待。

entries.definition: All the people who are able to work in a country or company.
entries.definitionCN: 一个国家或公司里所有能工作的人。

entries.definition: The people who are paid to work for an employer.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇于雇主、领取报酬工作的人。

entries.definition: A team of people working together, especially on a ship or aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 一起工作的一队人，尤指船或飞机上的全体人员。

normalIntro.en: The word is a French adjective sitting in a noun's chair, and its whole family runs back to the Latin mask.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是坐在名词位置上的法语形容词，而它的整个词族都要回到拉丁语的「面具」那里。

normal.en: Personnel is the noun use of a French adjective meaning personal, so it names persons rather than things.
normal.cn: personnel 是法语中意为「个人的」那个形容词当名词用，所以它指人而不指物。

normal.en: The ending -el is French; English personal uses -al, and that one letter is the main reason the two words are so easily confused.
normal.cn: 词尾 -el 来自法语；英语的 personal 用 -al，这一个字母的差别正是两词极易混淆的主因。

normal.en: As a collective noun it normally takes no plural, and one worker is a member of the personnel, not a personnel.
normal.cn: 作为集合名词，它通常不加复数；单独一个人要说成「人员中的一员」，而不能直接说成一个人。

normal.en: Personnel department shortened to personnel is a metonymy: the office is named after the people it manages.
normal.cn: 把「人事部门」缩成 personnel 是转喻：办公室被按它所管理的人来命名。

normal.en: In military reports personnel is the count on the roll, so losses are reported as personnel losses rather than as individual names.
normal.cn: 在军事报告里，personnel 就是名册上的数目，所以损失按「人员损失」统计，而不逐个列名字。

abstract.en: Think of a wall of name tags: the word never points at one tag, only at the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一整面名牌墙：这个词从不指向某一块名牌，只指向整面墙。

abstract.en: A French adjective walked into English and sat down as a noun; the stress still falls on the last syllable, as in French.
abstract.cn: 一个法语形容词走进英语，坐下当了名词；重音至今落在最后一个音节上，和法语一样。

abstract.en: One word covers both the people and the office that counts them, because paperwork always follows people.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指人，也指清点人的办公室，因为文书总是跟在人后面。

examples.en: All personnel must show their badges at the gate.
examples.cn: 所有员工都必须在大门口出示工牌。

examples.en: She was transferred to personnel after five years on the shop floor.
examples.cn: 在车间干了五年之后，她被调到了人事部门。

examples.en: Additional medical personnel were sent to the region.
examples.cn: 更多医疗人员被派往该地区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕搜人」——公司最怕搜不到合用的人，于是设了 personnel（人事部门）。

root: 来自拉丁语 persona（面具、角色、人）派生的形容词 personalis，经法语形容词 personnel 转为名词，指「属于某个机构的一群人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body of people attached to an organization; from that one collective sense grow the office that manages them, the roll of a military unit, and any named group of workers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是依附于某个机构的一群人；由这一个集合义长出管理他们的办公室、部队名册，以及任何被点名的一类专业工作者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of name tags, each one standing for a person who is on duty.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面挂满名牌的墙，每块名牌后面都有一个在岗的人。

branches.en: a wall of name tags in a lobby
branches.cn: 大厅里一整面名牌墙

branches.en: a hospital corridor full of staff in different uniforms
branches.cn: 医院走廊里穿不同制服的各类人员

branches.en: a queue outside a glass door with files stacked behind it
branches.cn: 玻璃门前排着队，门后堆着一摞摞档案

branches.en: a list of names read aloud at roll call
branches.cn: 点名时被逐个念出的名单

branches.en: paperwork travelling from a barracks to an office
branches.cn: 文件从营房一路送到办公室

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin noun for a mask, its adjective, and a French ending that let the adjective become a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示面具的拉丁名词、它的形容词，以及一个让形容词变成名词的法语词尾共同构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: adjectival ending kept in the noun
items.meaningCN: 保留在名词里的形容词词尾

definition_zh: 观点；视角；透视法；洞察力；远景
definition_en: a particular way of seeing or thinking about something, the art of showing depth on a flat surface, or the ability to judge things in proportion
core_image: 站在一个固定的位置透过窗框看出去：位置一换，看到的东西就重排。
scene: 在农夫眼里，这场旱灾是灾难；在水库管理者眼里，却是喘息之机。From the perspective of a farmer, the drought is a disaster; from the reservoir's, it is a reprieve.
sceneCN: 这里 perspective 是「看问题的角度」（第 1 个义项：视角、观点）；句意：从农民的角度看，这场干旱是灾难；从水库的角度看，却是喘息之机。场景要点：干裂的田、下降的水位标尺；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观点；视角；透视法；洞察力；远景

collocations.zh: 正确看待某事；把某事放到应有的比例中

senses.title: A point of view
senses.definition: a particular way of looking at or thinking about something, shaped by where you stand
senses.definitionCN: 由于所处位置而形成的看或思考某事的特定方式
senses.example: The novel tells the same event from three perspectives.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说从三个视角讲述同一件事。
senses.why: Latin perspicere meant 'to look through'. Perspective is the view you get from one position, as if looking through a particular opening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 perspicere 意为“看穿、看透”。perspective 就是从某一个位置透过特定开口所得到的视野。

senses.title: The ability to judge proportion
senses.titleCN: 分寸感：知道什么更重要
senses.definition: the ability to see how important things really are in relation to each other
senses.definitionCN: 看出事物之间真实轻重关系的能力
senses.example: Losing one game gave the team a sense of perspective.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉一场比赛反而让球队有了分寸感。
senses.why: Depth in a drawing comes from things being the right size relative to distance. Judging importance is the same skill applied to life.
senses.whyCN: 画面中的纵深，来自物体相对于距离的正确大小。判断重要性，是把同一种本事用在生活上。

senses.title: Art: the geometry of depth
senses.titleCN: 透视法：让平面显出纵深
senses.definition: the technique of representing three-dimensional space and depth on a flat surface
senses.definitionCN: 在平面上表现三维空间与纵深的技法
senses.example: The fresco uses linear perspective to draw the eye down the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画用线性透视把视线引向走廊深处。
senses.why: Renaissance painters formalized the idea that parallel lines converge to a vanishing point. Seeing 'through' the canvas is the literal source.
senses.whyCN: 文艺复兴画家把“平行线汇聚于消失点”形式化。透过画布“看进去”，正是这个词的字面来源。

senses.title: A distant view
senses.definition: a view, especially a wide or distant one, seen from a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 从某一地点看到的景色，尤指开阔或辽远的
senses.example: The ridge offers a perspective of the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊上能看到整个山谷的远景。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense in English: what is seen from here, extending away from the viewer.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最古老的物理义：从这里看出去、向远处铺开的东西。

senses.title: A considered opinion on a matter
senses.definition: a considered attitude or evaluation of a subject, often one among several
senses.definitionCN: 对某主题经过思考的态度或评价，常为多种之一
senses.example: We need the perspective of someone outside the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要一位行业外人士的看法。
senses.why: The visual metaphor becomes argumentative: a standpoint is a place you stand, and what you see from there is your opinion.
senses.whyCN: 视觉比喻变成论辩性的：立场就是你站的地方，从那里看到的东西就是你的观点。

senses.title: Psychology: taking another's viewpoint
senses.titleCN: 换位思考：站到别人的位置
senses.definition: in psychology, the capacity to understand another person's point of view
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中理解他人视角的能力
senses.example: Perspective-taking improves negotiation outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 换位思考能改善谈判结果。
senses.why: The word is used literally here: you imagine standing where the other stands, and the scene rearranges itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里用的是字面义：你想象站到对方所站的位置，整个场景就重新排列了。

senses.title: Proportion restored: in perspective
senses.titleCN: 比例复原：把事放回它的尺寸
senses.definition: in the phrase in perspective, shown at its true relative size or importance
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in perspective，表示按真实的相对大小或重要性来看
senses.example: The loss looks small when seen in perspective.
senses.exampleCN: 从整体比例看，这点损失显得很小。
senses.why: In a correct drawing, near things are large and far things small. Seeing something 'in perspective' is seeing it at the size its distance deserves.
senses.whyCN: 在正确的画里，近的大、远的小。把某事“in perspective”看，就是按它的距离应得的大小去看。

senses.title: Geometry: projection from a viewpoint
senses.titleCN: 投影法：从视点投出去的几何
senses.definition: in geometry, the system that projects a scene onto a plane from a chosen point
senses.definitionCN: 几何中从选定视点把场景投射到平面上的体系
senses.example: Perspective projection distorts parallel lines, unlike orthographic projection.
senses.exampleCN: 与正交投影不同，透视投影会使平行线产生畸变。
senses.why: The artistic technique becomes a mathematical one: a chosen eye point and a plane, with straight lines from one to the other.
senses.whyCN: 艺术技法变成了数学体系：一个选定的眼点、一个平面，以及从一点到另一点的直线。

intro.en: Perspective is Latin perspicere 'to look through' turned into a noun. English first used it for the science of sight, then for the painter's technique, and only later for a mental point of view.
intro.cn: perspective 是拉丁语 perspicere“看穿”名词化的结果。英语先用它指视觉的科学，再指画家的技法，最后才指心里的观点。

items.en: Specere meant 'to look, see'. It is the root behind spectacle, inspect, respect, and perspective.
items.cn: specere 意为“看、看见”。它是 spectacle、inspect、respect、perspective 的词根。

items.en: Perspicere was per- 'through' + specere 'look': 'to see through, look at closely, perceive clearly'.
items.cn: perspicere 是 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”：“看透、仔细看、清楚感知”。

items.en: Perspectiva was the medieval Latin term for the science of optics, literally 'the things of seeing through'.
items.cn: perspectiva 是中古拉丁语对光学的称呼，字面是“看穿的诸事”。

items.en: English takes perspective in the 14th century as the name of the optical science. It is a learned term before it is an everyday one.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 perspective，作为光学学科的名称。它先是学术用语，后才进入日常。

items.en: The artistic sense, the technique of showing depth on a flat surface, is recorded by the 1590s. The scientific name becomes a painter's tool.
items.cn: 艺术义（在平面上表现纵深的技法）于 16 世纪 90 年代见于记录。学科名称变成了画家的工具。

items.en: The sense 'a view from a place' is recorded by the 1660s; the figurative 'mental point of view' by 1762. The metaphor of standing somewhere and looking is fully in place.
items.cn: “从某处看到的景色”义于 17 世纪 60 年代见于记录；比喻性的“心理观点”义于 1762 年。站在某处张望的比喻至此完全成形。

note.en: The first group shares the specere 'look' root; the second collects words for a way of seeing or judging.
note.cn: 第一组共享 specere“看”词根；第二组收“看事物的方式”类词。

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand things. It comes from the same perspicere but describes a person, not a viewpoint.
entries.definitionCN: 观察敏锐、理解快的。它同出 perspicere，但描述人，而不是视角。

entries.definition: having a ready insight into things; mentally sharp. A formal adjective from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 对事物有敏锐洞察力的；心智锐利的。同出那个拉丁动词的正式形容词。

entries.definition: a possibility of a future event, or a view ahead. Pro- 'forward' + specere 'look'; the direction is forward, not through.
entries.definitionCN: 未来事件的可能性，或前方的景色。pro-“向前”+ specere“看”；方向是向前，不是穿透。

entries.definition: relating to perspective or to a point of view
entries.definitionCN: 与透视或视角有关的（由 perspective 派生）

entries.definition: a person's opinion or way of thinking. It is the everyday equivalent of perspective and lacks the art and depth senses.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的意见或思考方式。它是 perspective 的日常对应词，没有艺术与纵深的义项。

entries.definition: a position from which a subject is considered, often in debate. It keeps the physical 'standing place' image openly.
entries.definitionCN: 考虑某主题时所处的立场，常用于论辩。它明着保留“站立之处”的意象。
